items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: And, of course, I had Frank Jackie and Albert Martin and Cottrell in charge of most of the business.

ctx.x: Mm-hmm. I guess that would attract people's attention and everything. That's right. Well, how often did you rehearse with that band?

Every time we could get a chance. You know, being a traveling band on the road and you stay up all night, you have to pick the times. And the times you were playing, maybe you had a couple of dates or you had a couple of days lay off. Well, I would call it a rehearsal and we'd rehearse that way. Or, if the guy, someone had heard an arrangement or a song they wanted to put an arrangement on, he would write it at intervals. And he'd let me know when it was ready. And, of course, I had Frank Jackie and Albert Martin…
Mm-hmm. What would be a business manager, then?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-06-06
items.q: Now here's the band that I left New Orleans with, Paul.

ctx.x: He does. Well Beansy was here, Beansy met him.
Incidentally both of them in the same. Now here's the band that I left New Orleans with, Paul. Yeah.
I know you want to see this. Now we'll try to recall some of these names. I'll help you.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1974-01-01
items.q: in the band. They had names. Everyone had a nickname. For instance, I was twenty years old. I was the old man. And then of course, Geechee, I told you, he was right. And then, uh, Albert Martin was called Fats. And of course, Nicky got his name, Nicky.

ctx.x: Well, supposing some of the musicians would be talking about your coat or your tie. They'd say, watch it say the hawk's going to get it. They'd be having a cue to get hold of whatever it was, whoever the hawk was. I imagine somebody knew who the hawk was but they never knew. And then they used to call her, if a chick wasn't a nice looking chick, they would call her Taylor. And then she was not such a nice looking gal. What do you call her? Well, they call her a good looking chick. That's a nice looking Taylor.…
So, I guess, unless you can make something else, we'd better turn it up. We're almost to the end of the tape. Okay, thank you. Goodnight, Nicky. Goodnight.
